nodes.name: KBr salt-assisted annealing
nodes.procedure: To experimentally probe the prediction, the RE-RuO2-x – Ov (REα=Smα, Nd and Lu) catalysts with an asymmetric RE–O–Ru unit were synthesized using a modified KBr salt-assisted method. Typically, a finely ground mixture of Ru(acac)3, RE(acac), and KBr was annealed at 450 °C under air. After removing KBr, the RE-RuO2-x–Ov nanosheets were obtained (Experimental details are provided in the ESI†). The KBr salt acted as a sacrificial template to guide the oriented growth of RE-RuO2-x-Ov nanosheets and ensure their uniform distribution and high surface area. For comparison, the RE-free RuO2–Ov catalyst was also synthesized by employing the same method.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in acidic media
nodes.source_text: a two-electrode electrolyzer with Sm–RuO2−x–Ov as the anode and Pt/C as the cathode was used for overall water splitting in acidic media. Remarkably, the polarization curve for water splitting exhibits a low cell voltage of 1.44 V at 10 mA cm−2

nodes.characterization_summary: Rutile-phase RuO2 (110), (101), (211) facets with (110) peak negative shift due to larger RE atomic radius; no RE_xO_y peaks observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Three prominent diffraction peaks were well indexed to the (110), (101) and (211) facets of rutile-phase RuO2 (PDF# 40-1290) and no distinct diffraction peaks of RE_xO_y species were observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: RE molar ratio approximately 6 at% with uniform elemental distribution across RuO2 matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectra (EDS) show the molar ratio of RE in RE-RuO2-x–Ov samples of approximately 6 at%.

nodes.characterization_summary: RE content confirmed at approximately 6 at%, consistent with EDS results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in agreement with the inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) results in Table S1.

nodes.characterization_summary: 2D sheet-like morphology with rough and dense surfaces for both Sm-RuO2-x-Ov and RuO2-Ov.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of both Sm-RuO2-x-Ov and RuO2–Ov samples exhibit two-dimensional (2D) sheet-like morphology with rough and dense surfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: (110) lattice spacing of Sm-RuO2-x-Ov is 0.330 nm vs 0.320 nm for RuO2, confirming Sm substitution and lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the (110) lattice spacing of Sm-RuO2-x-Ov (0.330 nm) is larger than that of RuO2 (0.320 nm), demonstrating the lattice expansion due to the substitution of Sm for Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: Sm element signal confirms successful incorporation into RuO2 lattice, substituting Ru sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The signal of Sm element is also observed by the electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) spectrum, which further verifies the successful involvement of Sm atoms into the lattice of RuO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS: peaks at 529.1 eV (OL), 530.9 eV (Ov, shifted higher BE vs RuO2-Ov), 532.3 eV (Oad); Ov/OL ratio 1.77 (Sm-RuO2-x-Ov) vs 1.36 (RuO2-Ov); Ru 3p3/2 XPS: Ru3+ at 462.5 eV, Ru4+ at 465.2 eV with higher Ru3+/Ru4+ ratio in Sm-doped sample; Sm 3d5/2 at 1082.93 eV, 3d3/2 at 1110.17 eV (Sm3+).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution O 1s XPS spectrum of Sm–RuO2-x–Ov shown in Fig. 3a can be deconvoluted into three peaks at 529.1, 530.9 and 532.3 eV... For the Ru 3p3/2 spectra shown in Fig. 3c, the fitted peaks at 462.5 and 465.2 eV can be indexed to Ru3+ and Ru4+ species... In the high-resolution Sm 3d spectrum, the Sm 3d5/2 and Sm 3d3/2 spin-orbit peaks are found at two distinct binding energies of 1082.93 eV and 1110.17 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Stronger symmetric EPR signal at g=2.003 for Sm-RuO2-x-Ov than RuO2-Ov, demonstrating increased Ov concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Sm-RuO2-x-Ov shows a stronger symmetric EPR signal at g = 2.003 than that of RuO2–Ov, demonstrating an obvious increase in Ov concentration after the incorporation of Sm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES: adsorption threshold adjacent to RuO2, Ru oxidation state ~3.83 (Ru4+/Ru3+ mix); Sm L3-edge XANES: decreased white line intensity at 6722 eV vs Sm2O3, Sm oxidation state +2.6 indicating electron donation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru K-edge spectra shown in Fig. 3d demonstrate that the adsorption threshold position of the doped sample is higher than that of the Ru foil but adjacent to that of RuO2... The oxidation state of Ru in Sm-RuO2-x-Ov is calculated to be approximately 3.83... For Sm L3-edge adsorption, the Sm-RuO2-x-Ov presents the decreased white line intensity at 6722 eV, demonstrating that Sm deviates from high-valent Sm3+... the calculated oxidation state of Sm (+2.6).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-O bond length elongated; Ru-O coordination number 5.3 vs 6 in RuO2; Ru-O-Ru/Sm at 3.25 Å confirms Sm-Ru interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The best-fit results confirm the lower coordination number of 5.3 for Ru-O in Sm-RuO2-x-Ov than that of standard RuO2 (ΔCN = 6).

nodes.characterization_summary: Eg symmetrical vibration of Ru(OH)2 at ~523 cm-1 appears at 1.35 V vs RHE then disappears; Ru4+-O at 430 cm-1, Ru3+-O at 588 cm-1; higher I588/I430 ratio (~0.87 vs ~0.85) indicates more Ru3+ species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: with the bias electrode potential reaching 1.35 V versus RHE, the Sm-RuO2-x-Ov electrode exhibits the Eg symmetrical vibration scattering of Ru(OH)2 at ca. 523 cm-1, but it rapidly decreases and disappears at more positive voltages... two strong Raman bands at about 430 and 588 cm-1... can be assigned to Ru4+-O bonds and Ru3+-O bonds, respectively... the Sm-RuO2-x-Ov presents a higher intensity ratio (about 0.87) than that of RuO2–Ov (about 0.85).
